segments.voice: Yesterday, a grandfather's story handed over on a recording: ask thine elders. The story stays. Today, the ideas, all of them, in one breath.
screen: `THE STORY STAYS.` → `THE IDEAS, IN ONE BREATH.`

segments.voice: A goodbye dinner at Owen's house. Above the sink hangs a painted wooden sign that was Grandma June's: Do unto others. Noa reads it twice over the pot roast, and something clicks. She's heard this before, in a different voice. Owen's mom catches her looking and asks, warmly: that's basically a Jewish idea too, isn't it? Noa freezes. It's a fair question, and the honest answer has two halves.
screen: `A SIGN ABOVE THE SINK.` → `DO UNTO OTHERS.` → `AN ANSWER IN TWO HALVES.`

segments.voice: The question, then: can a whole tradition's thought fit in one sentence? The Talmud tells of a man who asked Hillel to teach him the entire Torah while he stood on one foot. Hillel answered, in our words: what is hateful to you, don't do to your neighbor. That's the whole Torah; the rest is commentary. Now go and learn. Look back at this path's thought, and that last line holds it all. The law, argued page by page in the Talmud. Philosophy, Maimonides reasoning his way toward God. Mysticism, the Kabbalists reading light into every letter. The movements, each finding its own way to live it. And character, the slow work of becoming kind. All of it is the commentary; all of it is go and learn. Now the first half of Noa's answer, the shared part. In Owen's Bible, in Matthew, Jesus says it this way, in the King James words: "all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets." Both teachers say one rule sums up the whole. Both stand near the same verse in Leviticus: "thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself." The second half, the honest difference. Hillel puts it as what not to do, and then sends the man off to study. In Matthew it's what to do, a teaching of Jesus, the one Owen's family follows. Neither line needs the other to be smaller.
screen: `THE WHOLE TORAH ON ONE FOOT.` · `THE REST IS COMMENTARY: GO LEARN.` · `MATTHEW: DO EVEN SO TO THEM.` · `SHARED GROUND, TWO VOICES.` · then, large: `THE IDEAS STAY.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write one idea from this path that changed how you live, in a single sentence, in your own words. Under it, write three more words: go and learn. Read both lines back once.
screen: `ONE IDEA THAT CHANGED YOU.` · `ONE SENTENCE, YOUR WORDS.` · `UNDER IT: GO AND LEARN.`
